To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the p s p relationship in AM processes is highly complex, and the use of digital twin models, either physics driven or data driven, can be an effective approach for understanding and predicting this relationship.

(i) physics and data driven approaches can be used to model the p s p relationship, (ii) the physics and data driven models have their advantages and limitations, (iii) the physics driven models are computationally expensive and require calibration, while the data driven models are computable with a large number of input variables but are not interpretable.
(1) Physics based models can provide a better understanding of AM process-structure-property relationships, but are computationally expensive.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of physics and data based methods to model the p s p relationship in metal AM.
the modeling of the p s ps relationships and how they are affected by the process parameters.
the development of physics based modeling tools for additive manufacturing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of both physics and data driven models is necessary to fully understand the p s p relationship in metal AM.
physics driven models are still needed to advance the understanding of p s p relationships and to guide the development of data driven models.
the future of p s p relationships modeling will be a hybrid of physics and data models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of digital twin models for the understanding of the complex p s p relationships can be beneficial in metal AM.
the use of physics driven and data based models in metal additive manufacturing is complementary.
physics driven methods provide a deeper insight into the process structure property linkages, while data driven methods provide a faster and more cost effective way of predicting these relationships.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the two modeling approaches should be used in synergy to advance the understanding of p s p relationships and to enable a better design of metal AM processes.

the two approaches are complementary and that a hybrid model that uses both physics driven and machine learning methods is needed to fully understand and predict the complex p s p relationships that are observed in metal AM.
the future of metal AM will be in the combination of data and physics driven methods to understand the p s p relationship.
